facts.text: Coyoacán’s name comes from Nahuatl, meaning ‘place of those who own coyotes,’ a nod to its pre‑Hispanic roots.
During colonial times, Coyoacán served as the first capital of the Viceroyalty and later stood guard against the Mexican‑American War.
Hernán Cortés and his troops established the first municipal council in Coyoacán after conquering the area.
The borough’s cultural center hosts three art galleries—Alfredo Ramos Martínez, Guillermo Kahlo, and Miguel Álvarez Acosta—each showcasing temporary exhibitions.
Coyoacán also houses the Instituto del Derecho de Asilo y las Libertades Públicas, founded in 1990, which champions asylum rights.
